title: Kestrel Health POC quality & load scoping - kickoff
next_steps: Redwood: send POC template + golden prompts spreadsheet (by 2026-11-09)
Kestrel: share representative dataset and expected QPS profile (by 2026-11-10)
SE to run baseline on 1k messages and post results (by 2026-11-16)
Schedule deep-dive on security controls with Kestrel infra (week of 2026-11-16)
action_items: Marco Ruiz: prepare benchmark config + sample scripts (due 2026-11-12)
Aisha Khan: export 2 weeks of anonymized logs + top 200 prompt examples (due 2026-11-10)
Lina Park: share pricing anchors and Dedicated capacity options (due 2026-11-09)
Tom Bunn: confirm network egress constraints and VPC peering possibility (due 2026-11-12)
summary: Kickoff for a 6-week POC to validate quality and load for a triage/recommendation assistant. Focus areas: golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination/format checks, scoring rubric, and baseline latency/cost tradeoffs. Team agreed to 50 golden prompts, 200 regression cases and an initial 1k message load run.
topics: POC scope; success criteria; workload sizing; golden prompt set; regression suite; hallucination detection; scoring weights and thresholds; timeline and deliverables; security and data flow
transcript:
[00:00] Lina (AE): Hi everyone thanks for hopping on. quick intro — I'm Lina from Redwood Inference, this is Marco, our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Aisha: doing well thanks, coffee in hand. excited to scoping this out, we have some pretty strict safety and accuracy goals.
[00:12] Marco (SE): great. quick note we usually run a quality eval with golden prompts + regression checks, and a small loadbench to get latency numbers. we'll tailor to your triage workflow.
[00:20] Tom: to set context, we route clinical messages to a human if the model isn't confident. primary metrics for us are hallucination rate, format compliance to our output schema, and latency under load.
[00:31] Sara: timeline wise product wants a pilot in ~6 weeks, but we're flexible if the eval shows more work.
[00:36] Lina: good. can we confirm stakeholders? Aisha you'll own accuracy evaluation, Tom on infra, Sara product sign-off.
[00:42] Aisha: correct.
[00:45] Marco: okay so proposed success criteria — preliminary: p50 latency under 200ms for standard prompts at 5 qps, hallucination rate < 1% on golden prompts, format compliance 99% (fields present + enum checks), and F1 for entity extraction > 0.88. those are starting numbers.
[01:05] Aisha: the <1% hallucination seems aggressive — how do you define hallucination? sometimes we get partial hallucinations where dates or dosages are wrong.
[01:13] Marco: good question. for this POC we'll define hallucination as any generated fact that contradicts the input context or invents unsupported medical claims. we'll detect via a combination of exact matching in regression tests and semantic checks using a verifier model. There will be manual review on borderline cases.
[01:28] Tom: for load, our expectations are around 10 qps peak but usually 3-5 qps. we need to validate cost at sustained 3 qps and burst to 10.
[01:37] Lina: sounds reasonable. we'll run two load profiles: steady 3 qps for 30 min and a burst test 10 qps for 5 min. SE note - we may run with Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity or hosted variant depending on latency.
[01:49] Speaker 6: is there an offline batch mode too? we have nightly jobs.
[01:52] Marco: yes we support batch embeddings and bulk rerank; for POC we focus online responses but we can include a nightly batch sanity check.
[01:59] Sara: about golden prompts — you mentioned 50, is that enough?
[02:03] Marco: 50 gold prompts across 5 intent buckets gives reasonable coverage; plus we'll make a 200-case regression suite drawn from historic logs. golden prompts are high-salience cases we expect 0 hallucination on. regression tests handle edge cases.
[02:16] Aisha: what about scoring? we need something simple for product to sign off.
[02:19] Marco: propose weighted scoring: 40% hallucination rate (lower is better), 25% format compliance, 20% entity extraction F1, 15% latency/cost penalty. we convert to a 0-100 score and require >= 85 to pass.
[02:33] Aisha: can you walk through an example?
[02:36] Marco: sure. if hallucination metric is 0.5% -> assign 95/100 on hallucination axis, format compliance 98% -> 98, F1 0.90 -> 90, latency penalty small -> 95; weighted sum leads to ~93.
[02:49] Lina: also note we recommend prefix caching for repeated prompts and smart batching. that drives down cost but has config tradeoffs. we'll document caching expectations.
[02:58] Tom: security — we need SOC2 type 2 and KMS integration, plus audit logs. do you provide key-in-cloud or customer-managed keys?
[03:06] Marco: for hosted we offer Redwood-managed KMS; for Private/VPC deployments we support customer-managed keys (HSM via KMS). we'll send the security pack and SOC2 report.
[03:16] Sara: any limitations on retention? compliance needs logs retained for 1 year.
[03:20] Lina: retention and log export configurable; for Private deployments you retain everything in your VPC. we'll note that in the security doc.
[03:27] Aisha: about hallucination detection automation — you mentioned a verifier model, is that another external call?
[03:31] Marco: could be local or a lightweight verifier. for the POC we can run a semantic similarity check and a small set of rule-based checks; manual review will triage the rest.
[03:40] Sara: how do we handle format checks? we have a strict JSON schema with nested fields.
[03:44] Marco: we'll validate with schema validators; if model returns malformed JSON we'll run a parse-and-retry policy for up to 2 attempts, then flag for human. counting those retries affects format compliance scoring.
[03:56] Aisha: ok. what's the plan for regression test updates? after the first run do we add failing cases to gold set?
[04:01] Marco: typical flow: golden prompts are stable high-priority tests; failing regression cases go into an expanding 'known-issues' list. some may graduate to golden prompts if they're high-severity.
[04:10] Lina: timings — SE will run baseline 1k messages in week 2, then a 10k run for cost projection in week 4, and final quality run before review week 6.
[04:20] Tom: can we include a private deployment trial for one week to validate networking?
[04:24] Lina: yes we can provision a short-lived Private environment or a Dedicated slice — we'll include options in the follow-up.
[04:31] Speaker 6 (unclear): do you have pre-built scripts for EMR-like logging?
[04:34] Marco: we have sample clients and a load harness — will share repo link.
[04:38] Sara: pricing conversation — we need rough numbers to compare to our internal GPU costs.
[04:42] Lina: I'll share pricing anchors and math for ded vs hosted. we typically show cost per 1k tokens and per inference at target latency.
[04:50] Aisha: any competitor caveats? we evaluated Anthropic and an in-house runtime; our in-house is fast but has hallucination problems.
[04:58] Marco: noted. for tooling we'll also provide per-route latency and token-cost breakdowns so you can see unit economics.
[05:05] Lina: ok let's recap next steps — Marco will run baseline and share scripts; I'll send POC template + security pack; Aisha/Tom will share sample data and constraints.
[05:15] Tom: perfect. thanks all.
[05:18] Sara: thanks, talk soon.
[05:21] Lina: bye everyone.
